summary: Current Arbitrum own collateral ledger and queued AMLP liquidity; not merely an offchain-exchange deposit helper.

lifecycleEvidence.reason: Current official product/docs describe live perpetual exchange and AMLP hybrid liquidity; current frontend binds AMLP manager and wallet/account funding addresses; public liquidity mode is enabled at observation. No categorical safety claim follows.

selectedFunctions.label: Antarctic Exchange deposit owned financial operation
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, liquidity, backing, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Existing grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory; all selected functions require zero native value.

Arbitrum FundingVault and AMLP manager are nonproxy deployed contracts with Sourcify exact_match creation/runtime records. The current official application bundle binds these addresses and AMLP; manager inPrivateMode() was false, FundingVault supportedTokens(USDT) and isManager(AMLP manager) were true at observation, not ongoing availability guarantees. Governance, supported assets, handlers and dependencies remain mutable.

FundingVault deposit pulls caller tokens and increments balanceOf[token][msg.sender]; withdraw debits that same owned ledger and returns to caller. This is an internal financial collateral ledger, not a bare token transfer helper. Only supported tokens, positive amount and sufficient caller/vault balances qualify. Native token units apply (current Arbitrum USDT has 6 decimals). No trading-wallet forwarding method is admitted.

AMLP addLiquidity pulls caller USDT and queues userDeposits[msg.sender]; addLiquidityFromVault debits caller FundingVault ledger through its authorized manager and queues the same owned request. Observed minimum is 10,000,000 USDT units (10 USDT). Neither immediately mints AMLP or supplies a caller minimum-share/price bound. Handler settlement later uses operator-supplied TVL, floors USDT*existingSupply/TVL (initial shares use amount*1e30/1e18) and forwards USDT to configured exVault. AMLP has 18 decimals.

removeLiquidityToWallet/ToVault enqueue caller-owned AMLP by transferFrom and increment userWithdraws[msg.sender]. They do not pay out immediately. An existing admin-issued signature binds exactly msg.sender, AMLP amount, timestamp and nonce to this fixed request; caller cannot name a payer, executable target or arbitrary payload. Signature is financial request data, not a backend signing or wallet-authority grant; catalog generates none. Source checks timestamp < block time and timestamp > block time-removeLiquidityCooldown, with observed 604800-second window and per-user nonce consumption. Source signature omits chain/contract domain separation; cross-deployment replay risk is not ruled out.

ToWallet versus ToVault is encoded only in the emitted request type, not the signed message. Actual redemption amount and destination route are later chosen by admitted-neither handler batch settlement, which burns queued AMLP and returns handler-supplied USDT redemption amount either to that user or their FundingVault ledger. Cancellation is handler-only, not a caller guarantee. No guaranteed quote, payout date, return, principal preservation or complete self-service exit. Admin/operator batch functions, signer checks, role grants and arbitrary tradingAddress transfers are excluded.

> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://docs.antarctic.exchange/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://docs.antarctic.exchange/technical-framework/hybird-lp-model.md).

# Hybird LP Model

AX uses a hybrid liquidity model that combines on-chain guarantees with off-chain efficiency. Deposits and redemptions—covering stablecoins and the AMLP/AHLP vaults—are executed through smart contracts to preserve transparency and user protection, while off-chain components support performance and operational scalability where appropriate.

#### On-chain + Off-chain Design

AX’s liquidity system is built to keep the LP experience simple without sacrificing verifiability:

* **On-chain execution and auditability:** Core actions are enforced by smart contracts, and key interactions can be independently verified on-chain.
* **Off-chain efficiency:** Off-chain modules help manage complexity and improve throughput, enabling a smoother user experience while maintaining clear, rules-based behavior.

#### Liquidity Pool Stability & Protection

To reduce unnecessary churn and protect LPs during periods of volatility, AX applies a **Time Lock** on LP exits. This mechanism is designed to:

* discourage frequent in-and-out behavior that can destabilize pool performance,
* reduce negative externalities on long-term participants, and
* maintain fair, predictable liquidity conditions for the broader market.

Critical parameters related to liquidity operations are governed by transparent rules, with safeguards (including time-delayed changes where applicable) to ensure consistent and accountable system behavior.

# What is Antarctic?

Antarctic (AX) is a **decentralized perpetual futures exchange** designed to deliver **institutional-grade execution**, **low fees**, and **strong privacy guarantees**. AX combines **non-custodial settlement** with **transparent, rules-based market operations** to provide a trading venue that is **resilient**, **permissionless**, and aligned with the core principles of **on-chain finance**.

To support **consistent execution quality**, AX is built around **deep liquidity** and **efficient price discovery**. The protocol is engineered to **minimize adverse selection** and reduce the **structural disadvantages** often faced by retail traders, while maintaining **clear and auditable market behavior** for all participants.

AX aims to offer a **CEX-level user experience** without compromising the flexibility of **decentralized trading**. While the initial focus is **perpetuals**, the platform is designed to **expand its feature set over time**—prioritizing **performance**, **risk controls**, and product capabilities demanded by **active traders**.**alized trading.** While the initial focus is perpetuals, the platform is designed to expand its feature set over time—prioritizing performance, risk controls, and product capabilities demanded by active traders.

By contributing capital to our liquidity pools, you contribute to the depth of trading pairs and the efficiency of our network. In return, you will receive the yield. Liquidity providers earn x% of trading fees collected by the exchange. Before our TGE, LP contributors also receive ATTX tokens through a form of “boosted yield” based on your LP contribution. For example, if the native yield of our LP is 10%, you may receive an extra X% in ATTX token - boosting your yield
